title: Map Redwood overload error codes into OpenAI-compatible error objects
author: Brian Murphy
body: Context: The Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding rollout introduces stable overload semantics (429/503 + Redwood-specific error codes + Retry-After). For customers using the OpenAI-compatible endpoints, we need to surface the same semantics while preserving the OpenAI error envelope and not breaking existing client expectations (SDKs and common OSS clients assume `error.message`, `error.type`, `error.code` shapes and sometimes string-match on `rate_limit_exceeded`). This PR adds a deterministic mapping from Redwood overload codes (e.g. `OVERLOAD_ADMISSION_REJECTED`, `OVERLOAD_BREAKER_OPEN`, `OVERLOAD_RUNTIME_QUEUE_FULL`, `OVERLOAD_MEMORY_PRESSURE`) into OpenAI-style error objects, while keeping HTTP status codes and headers unchanged. Design goals: (1) keep existing retry behavior sane by using conventional `error.type` values (rate_limit_error / api_error / server_error) and stable messages; (2) preserve Redwood-specific detail via `error.code` (string) and a non-breaking `error.meta` payload; (3) never introduce a new top-level response shape; (4) ensure `Retry-After` is forwarded on 429/503 and exposed in the error payload as `error.retry_after_ms` for clients that don’t read headers. Mapping summary (high level): - 429 with Redwood overload codes -> OpenAI error `{ type: rate_limit_error, code: rate_limit_exceeded }` plus `meta.redwood_error_code=<original>` - 503 with breaker open / regional saturation -> OpenAI error `{ type: api_error, code: service_unavailable }` plus `meta.redwood_error_code` - streaming disconnects where we already terminate with compat error -> keep existing behavior; if we have a Redwood reason code, attach meta only (do not change message to avoid breaking clients that treat disconnects specially). Notable implementation details: - Added `toOpenAIError()` translator for Redwood error payloads, with a strict allowlist of fields to avoid leaking internal details. - Centralized the overload mapping table and added unit tests for all known overload reason codes + unknown/new codes (fallback path). - Added `Retry-After` forwarding into the compat layer and ensured we do not override gateway-provided values. - Added snapshot tests for the OpenAI error payload and an integration test that validates we maintain the previous message text for legacy 503 paths (non-overload). Rollout/compat: This is behind the existing OpenAI-compat versioned router. No behavior change for non-overload 4xx/5xx errors. For overload responses, clients will see more consistent `type`/`code`, with Redwood detail available in `error.meta.redwood_error_code` and `error.meta.redwood_overload_reason` where present. Docs follow-up is tracked separately (ENG-4832).
commits: compat/errors: add Redwood->OpenAI overload mapping table
compat/middleware: forward Retry-After and preserve status codes
tests: add overload mapping unit tests + snapshots
compat: attach meta.redwood_error_code without changing legacy messages
chore: tighten schema validation for Redwood error payloads
review_conversation: Amara Diallo: Can we confirm we’re not rewriting 503 bodies that currently come from the gateway when it’s not overload-protected? We had a couple customers parsing the message string (unfortunate but real).

Brian Murphy (author): Good call. Added a guard: we only apply the overload mapping when we detect Redwood overload code in the upstream JSON OR the `x-redwood-overload: true` hint header. Otherwise we preserve the existing compat error behavior and message. Added `legacy_503_message_preserved` integration test.
Jordan Lee: For unknown/new overload reason codes, what do we emit? We don’t want clients to treat it as rate_limit_exceeded if it’s actually a breaker open (503) case.

Brian Murphy (author): Unknown codes keep the upstream HTTP status as the source of truth. For 429 unknown -> rate_limit_error/rate_limit_exceeded; for 503 unknown -> api_error/service_unavailable. Meta includes the unknown Redwood code to aid debugging.
Monica Patel: Please make sure `error.code` remains a string (some OpenAI clients treat numeric codes as invalid). Also would be nice to expose Retry-After in the error object for SDKs.

Brian Murphy (author): `error.code` is a string in all paths. Added `error.retry_after_ms` (derived from Retry-After seconds header when present) but only when header exists; otherwise omitted to keep payload minimal.
Wei Chen: README update looks good. Minor wording: use 'Retry-After header' (capitalization) and clarify that `error.meta` is an extension used by Redwood.
Brian Murphy (author): Updated wording and added a short section documenting `error.meta.redwood_error_code` as a Redwood extension.
Amara Diallo: One more: please don’t include internal region/model identifiers in meta; we’ve had support asks but we shouldn’t leak routing internals.
Brian Murphy (author): Agreed. Meta allowlist is limited to Redwood public error codes and overload reason enums; explicitly dropped `region`, `pool`, `route_id` fields if present upstream.
release_notes: OpenAI-compatible endpoints now translate Redwood overload-protection errors into standard OpenAI error envelopes while preserving HTTP status codes and Retry-After; Redwood-specific overload codes are available via `error.meta.redwood_error_code`.
